name: consistency-violation-unreachable-memory
description: A task moved into a partition on a core that is DECLARED but from which the memory its component budgets is not reachable. It is `broken-reference-task-on-undeclared-partition.json`'s sibling one pass later: the same change set over a fixture that declares `PARTITION1` on `CORE1`, so both references resolve and what refuses the staged result is `hardware.unreachable-memory` — a `consistency-violation`, because every identity in the rule resolves and nothing is dangling. What is wrong is the DESIGN: the integrator has not declared that `CORE1` may use `RAM0`. Since contract `9.0.0` a task reaches its core through its partition, so the rule reads the core the task's partition is on.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model with a second core, `CORE1`, seeded beside `CORE0`, and an unrated partition `PARTITION1` on it. `RAM0` is accessible from `CORE0` alone; `Task_10ms` runs in `PARTITION0`, so on `CORE0`, and runs a runnable of `ExampleConsumerSWC`, which budgets `RAM0`. The change set moves the task into `PARTITION1`.

authorization.notes: The scope covers the address exactly, so the refusal is the model rule and not the authorization boundary. Note which way the safety guard does NOT point here: moving a task is not a safety act, and the edit that WOULD be one is the other repair — admitting `CORE1` to `RAM0.accessible`, which `examples/update-memory-accessible-and-threshold.json` carries as a `widen_access`.

input.intent: Move Task_10ms into the partition on the second core.

expected.notes: Three addresses, and they are the three legal repairs: move the task back into a partition whose core the memory admits, move its partition to such a core, or admit the core to the memory. The rule does not choose between them, exactly as `consistency-violation-second-processor.json` does not choose which processor to delete. The last address is the `accessible` FIELD and not a member of it — the three sibling `accessible` rules address a member because the member is there and is wrong, whereas here the repair adds a member that does not exist yet and has no address. What this refusal does NOT reach is the linker script: `hardware.unreachable-memory` reads whether the integrator DECLARED the memory reachable from that core, and nothing in the model expresses where a symbol is actually linked.
